title: Tree-nut granola on a dedicated line
body: When tree nuts are a declared ingredient and the line is dedicated (no peanut zoning overlap), declare tree_nut as present. Do not infer peanut presence from tree nuts. Cross-contact peanut requires a separate facility shared-line signal or a validated changeover gap.

title: Shared peanut line without validated changeover
body: A facility with peanut on a shared line and no validated changeover SOP on file must carry peanut as possible_cross_contact at Tier C (defaulted). A controlled SOP id on the facility upgrades this to a documented control; peanut may still appear as precautionary depending on swab evidence, but it is no longer an unmitigated default.

title: Oats milled on a shared wheat mill
body: Rolled oats are not wheat, but mills that also handle wheat commonly declare wheat cross-contact. Carry wheat as possible_cross_contact at the ingredient's stated tier. Do not upgrade oats to a wheat declaration.

title: Sulfites in dried fruit
body: Sulfites used to preserve raisins are a process aid, not a Big-9 allergen. Surface them on the pack as a process-aid notice. They do not count toward allergen-matrix presence for milk/egg/fish/shellfish/tree_nut/peanut/wheat/soy/sesame.

title: Soy lecithin as a minor additive
body: Soy lecithin is soy. Declare soy as present at the ingredient tier even at low recipe weight. Weight still counts toward the 80% Tier-A coverage rule.

title: Cocoa powder sector default — milk cross-contact
body: Absent a primary spec, cocoa powder defaults to possible milk cross-contact (shared confectionery lines). This is Tier C and defaulted. A dated supplier spec that explicitly states dedicated cocoa processing removes the default.

title: Honey has no safe sector default
body: Honey has no reliable sector default for allergen or process-aid claims. Missing honey specs are gaps, not Tier-C fills. Do not invent a 'none' declaration.

title: Recent oil supplier switch
body: A recent supplier switch with no spec sheet on file is a gap. Do not copy the previous oil supplier's allergen statement onto the new supplier.

title: Kids pouch — higher disclosure bar
body: Products intended for young children should not ship a screening pack while intended_market or label_claims are gapped. Flag these as blocking gaps even if recipe-weight coverage would otherwise pass.

title: Sesame is a regulated allergen in EU and US
body: Sesame must appear on the allergen matrix whenever it is a declared ingredient. Harbor Pack's tahini SKU is sesame-present at Tier A when a spec sheet exists.
